donnees.titre: Four-year corneal hysteresis and intraocular pressure outcomes after ab-interno canaloplasty with phacoemulsification in glaucoma.
donnees.resume:
PURPOSE: To evaluate longitudinal changes in intraocular pressure (IOP), medication burden, and corneal biomechanical parameters over 4 years following phacoemulsification combined with ab-interno canaloplasty (AbiC) in patients with primary open-angle glaucoma.
METHODS: This retrospective, longitudinal, non-comparative cohort study included 40 eyes from 28 patients. Clinical data were collected preoperatively and up to 4 years postoperatively. Continuous outcomes, including absolute and relative IOP reduction, were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Secondary analyses included Kaplan-Meier estimates based on predefined IOP thresholds (≤ 18 mmHg), evaluated both with and without medications. Sensitivity analyses were performed using alternative thresholds (≤ 15 and ≤ 21 mmHg).
RESULTS: Mean IOP decreased significantly over time (global p = 0.009), with the greatest reduction at one year (- 1.71 mmHg; 95% CI - 2.94 to - 0.47; p = 0.003). Although attenuation was observed at later time points, IOP remained numerically below baseline through year four. Medication burden decreased significantly at one year (- 1.48 medications; 95% CI - 1.85 to - 1.10; p < 0.001), followed by gradual reintroduction. Corneal hysteresis increased after surgery and remained significantly higher than baseline during follow-up (p < 0.001). The cumulative probability of maintaining IOP ≤ 18 mmHg was 85.0% at four years, whereas medication-free control was 10.0%. No sight-threatening complications occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: Phacocanaloplasty was associated with an early significant reduction in IOP with partial attenuation over time, while remaining numerically below baseline during long-term follow-up. The increase in corneal hysteresis is consistent with a favorable postoperative biomechanical profile.
